title: Highveld Cold Storage

sentences.text: You are a first-year audit manager at Dlamini & Associates Inc., responsible for the external audit of Highveld Cold Storage (Pty) Ltd (Highveld) for the year ended 30 June 2026.
Highveld operates large refrigerated logistics warehouses across Gauteng, storing perishable pharmaceutical products and export agricultural produce.
Highveld has been an audit client of Dlamini & Associates for nine consecutive years, generating 18% of the audit firm's total annual fee income.
The engagement partner, Johan Dlamini, went to university with Highveld's Managing Director and frequently plays golf with him.
During final analytical procedures, you discover that Highveld breached its debt service coverage covenant on a R45 million facility with Apex Bank on 15 June 2026.
The Managing Director instructed the financial manager to backdate a R12 million customer storage deposit receipt to hide the covenant breach from Apex Bank.
The financial manager complied with the Managing Director's instruction because he feared losing his annual performance bonus.

When you raised the backdated entry with Johan Dlamini, he sighed and said: "Highveld is our biggest client; if we qualify the audit report or delay signing, they will fire us and our firm cannot survive that loss."
Johan instructed you to sign off the working papers and treat the R12 million backdating as an "immaterial timing difference".
Highveld's Social and Ethics Committee has not met during the financial year, in direct contravention of the Companies Act.
You are considering whether this matter constitutes a Reportable Irregularity in terms of section 45 of the Auditing Profession Act (APA).

required: Evaluate the ethical dilemma facing you, as the audit manager, in terms of the SAICA Code of Professional Conduct. In your answer, do not discuss Reportable Irregularities.

recall.question: What kind of business is Highveld Cold Storage?
options: A refrigerated logistics and warehousing company
A pharmaceutical manufacturer
A cold-room construction contractor
An agricultural export trader

recall.question: What is your role?
options: The audit manager on Highveld's external audit
Highveld's financial manager
A credit analyst at Apex Bank
Chair of Highveld's Social and Ethics Committee

recall.question: What did the client do that created the problem?
options: Backdated a receipt to hide a loan covenant breach from the bank
Failed to pay the audit fee
Sold warehouses without board approval
Refused the auditors access to its records

recall.question: What did the engagement partner tell you to do?
options: Sign off and treat the backdated entry as an immaterial timing difference
Report the Managing Director to IRBA
Resign from the audit
Ask Apex Bank for a covenant waiver
Evaluate under the Code: the threats to the fundamental principles, how significant they are, what you must do, and a conclusion
A discussion of whether the Managing Director committed fraud under the Companies Act
A legal assessment of whether Apex Bank can cancel the facility
A list of audit procedures to test the backdated receipt
shape.why: "Evaluate" means weighing, not listing: name each threat and the principle at risk, say how serious it is and whether a safeguard can deal with it, and end with a conclusion on what you must do.

options.text: Leave out whether a Reportable Irregularity has occurred under the Auditing Profession Act
Use the SAICA Code of Professional Conduct
Discuss the Social and Ethics Committee's failure to meet
Evaluate the financial manager's bonus scheme
Report the matter to Apex Bank

directions.why: The required carries an exclusion: anything on Reportable Irregularities or section 45 earns nothing, however good. The Social and Ethics Committee and the financial manager's bonus are in the case to tempt you; neither is your dilemma.

options: You, the audit manager: what the partner's instruction means for your own ethics
The Managing Director: whether backdating the receipt was ethical
The financial manager: whether he should have followed the instruction
Apex Bank: whether it was misled
lens.why: "The ethical dilemma facing you, as the audit manager" sets the lens. Judging the Managing Director's or the financial manager's conduct answers a different question. The firm's fee dependence and the partner's friendship count only as the reasons for the pressure on you.

rows.point: Intimidation threat: the partner pressures you, under threat of losing the client, to sign off and call the backdating immaterial
Self-interest threat: fear of losing the firm's biggest client puts the firm's interests (and your own standing) ahead of objectivity
Fee dependence: 18% of the firm's fees from one client makes the self-interest threat significant, and explains the partner's pressure
Familiarity threat: nine years on the audit and the partner's close friendship with the Managing Director weaken professional scepticism
The backdating is deliberate manipulation to hide a covenant breach, so it is material by its nature whatever the amount; calling it an "immaterial timing difference" is not true
Integrity: signing off would knowingly associate you with false or misleading information
Objectivity and professional competence and due care: signing off without resolving the entry is not proper audit work
Action: refuse to sign off, document the matter and your discussion with the partner, and escalate inside the firm (ethics partner, engagement quality reviewer or firm leadership)

Conclusion: while the instruction stands, no safeguard reduces these threats to an acceptable level; if it is not reversed, you cannot be associated with the work (remove yourself from the engagement, take legal advice)
